albums.blurb: Guaraldi was a fixture of the San Francisco jazz scene when he cut this trio date for Fantasy with bassist Monty Budwig and drummer Colin Bailey, pairing interpretations of the Luiz Bonfá and Antônio Carlos Jobim music from the 1959 film Black Orpheus with a handful of originals. Its breakout success is what brought Guaraldi to the attention of TV producer Lee Mendelson, who hired him to score the Peanuts specials three years later.
albums.reception: The album's original "Cast Your Fate to the Wind" won the 1963 Grammy Award for Best Original Jazz Composition and climbed to No. 22 on the Billboard Hot 100.

albums.blurb: Withers' second album, released on Sussex in May 1972 and recorded with members of the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band, follows his Booker T. Jones-produced debut Just As I Am and marks the point where he took charge of his own leaner, funkier sound. It is home to "Lean on Me," "Use Me," and "Who Is He (And What Is He to You)?", and the 2009 documentary about Withers took its title from the record.
albums.reception: Still Bill reached No. 4 on the Billboard 200, while "Lean on Me" spent three weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 in July 1972 and "Use Me" peaked at No. 2.

albums.blurb: Ezra Collective is a London quintet led by drummer Femi Koleoso — also Gorillaz's touring drummer — with his brother TJ on bass, Joe Armon-Jones on keys, James Mollison on sax, and Ife Ogunjobi on trumpet; the band met as teenagers in the Tomorrow's Warriors youth jazz program. Their second album, released on Partisan in November 2022, folds Afrobeat, salsa, grime, and reggae into the group's jazz core, with guest turns from Sampa the Great, Kojey Radical, Nao, and Emeli Sandé.
albums.reception: It won the 2023 Mercury Prize, making Ezra Collective the first jazz act to take the award in the prize's history.
